chunks: From him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Karram ibn Amr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'If a man makes the private part of his slave-girl permissible for his brother,' he said, 'Yes, there is no objection; he has whatever he made permissible for him from her.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no objection / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on a master allowing another man to have sexual relations with his slave-girl?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifying that when a master grants his slave-girl to another man, the grantee acquires the specific rights of usage (*istimta'*) designated by the grantor. This highlights the flexibility of *milk al-yamin* (possession) rights in Shia jurisprudence, where the owner can transfer sexual access without transferring full ownership, a nuance distinct from the prohibition of *sharik* (sharing) in some other schools. The phrase 'he has what he made permissible for him' underscores that the scope of the grant is defined by the grantor's stipulation.
